survey: Image 4 shows a gold five-pointed sheriff star floating on a purple sunburst background, with no ground plane. Each point ends in a gold ball. A raised red cabochon gem sits in a round bezel at the centre. The bevelled ridges run from the centre to each tip and to each inner notch. The badge faces the viewer almost head-on. The gem bezel is a near-perfect circle, which means the face is not noticeably tilted. The balls are spheres, so they read correctly from any angle. The lighting and bevels agree on one frontal view.

errors.where: Star arms, especially the lower-left point
errors.what: The circular gem bezel shows the badge face-on, so the five arms should be about equal in length and evenly spaced. Instead the lower-left arm is about 30% shorter than the top and right arms, and the angles between arms are uneven. A tilt cannot explain this: the gem would turn into an ellipse, and the arm opposite the lower-left (the upper-right gap between the top and right arms) would shorten too, but those are the longest arms. The star is lopsided rather than foreshortened.

fix: Draw a symmetrical sheriff star seen straight on: five arms of equal length spaced evenly at 72 degrees, each ending in a same-size gold ball, with a round red gem centred exactly in the middle.
